2. The notifications bell icon: open it, confirm a real dropdown/panel renders (even if empty), doesn't error.

Theme toggle: click it repeatedly (dark→light→dark) on several different pages (dashboard, deploy, billing, settings) and confirm the WHOLE page — sidebar, topbar, main content, any open modal — consistently reflects the new theme with no leftover dark-mode or light-mode remnants anywhere, and reload the page after toggling to confirm the choice persists (pre-paint script should apply it before first render, no flash of the wrong theme).

Check the browser console around this specifically for any hydration mismatch warnings/errors (a real one was found and fixed here earlier today — confirm it's actually gone, don't just assume).
5. The cookie-consent banner and the live-chat widget bubble (bottom-right): confirm both render without errors and their buttons (Opt out / Got it, and the chat bubble) do something sensible.
6. The sidebar: with a long nav list open at a shorter browser window height (try 700px tall), confirm the nav scrolls internally without a visible scrollbar and without any hairline gap/artifact of a different color along its edges, in BOTH light and dark mode. Also check the sidebar in its collapsed/icon-only state (resize the browser to ~1000-1279px wide, which should show the compact icon rail instead of the full labeled sidebar) and in its fully-hidden mobile state (below ~1024px, should show a hamburger menu that opens a slide-out drawer).

8. Check the browser console for errors/React hydration warnings throughout all of the above.

Report back with concrete, specific findings only (component/file names if identifiable, exact repro steps, screenshot paths under /tmp if saved). If something genuinely works, say so — don't invent findings. Do NOT fix anything yourself, this is discovery only.

# v2 design sandbox

The real Nxeon codebase, isolated, carrying the Nexion design. Nothing here can
reach a customer, a hypervisor or a payment processor.

- **URL** — https://v2.q4w8zt3ky6vn2sm.nxeon.cloud
- **Login** — `admin@nxeon.local`, password in `/root/nxeon-v2-credentials.txt`
- **Branch** — `design/v2`
- **Port** — 3021
- **Database** — `nxeon_v2` (its own role; prod's database is never opened)

`NXEON_SANDBOX=1`, and Proxmox / Stripe / registrar / SMTP all point at dead
endpoints, so provisioning and checkout can be exercised end to end without
anything actually being provisioned or charged.

## The edit → rebuild loop

This tree serves a **production build**, not the dev server. Nothing hot-reloads;
every change needs:

```bash
/opt/nxeon-v2/rebuild.sh
```

That stops the service, builds, and restarts ONLY if the build succeeded — a
failed build leaves the last working version serving rather than replacing it
with a broken one. It stops the service first because `next build` writes into
`.next` while the running server reads from it; building in place has already
taken this sandbox down once.

It skips the marketing site by default (137 of ~195 route files, for a section
this redesign does not touch). Build everything with:

```bash
NX_FULL=1 /opt/nxeon-v2/rebuild.sh
```

which is **mandatory before any staging or production pass**, where marketing
must be built and exercised.

### Why not the dev server

Measured on this box, same app: production build **0.66 GB**, dev server
**~4.5 GB and growing**. Spare memory here is counted against fifteen customer
VMs. The dev server also made pages genuinely slow to open — the browser was
unpacking 3,252 separate files per navigation — so the build is faster to USE
and only slower to CHANGE.

Build timings: full **373s**, without marketing **291s** (compile alone 132s ->
71s). The remainder is the type-check, which still sees every file.

Switching back to instant iteration is a one-line change to
`/etc/systemd/system/nxeon-v2-web.service` (`npm start` -> `npm run dev`).

### Why a page took a minute

Next's dev server compiles a route the first time it is requested, and this box
is a busy hypervisor with little spare memory, so that first hit is expensive —
`/dashboard` alone costs ~15s, the deploy wizard far more. You should never be
the one paying it.

**The warmer** (`nxeon-v2-warm.service`) walks the dashboard routes in the
background at idle priority after every restart, so the compile is already done
before you click. `requireUser()` runs *inside* the page, so an anonymous
request still triggers and caches the compile — the warmer needs no login.

**Not Turbopack.** `next dev --turbopack` looks like the obvious fix and is
roughly 5x faster, but its resolver rejects `fontkit` (pulled in by `pdfkit`,
which generates the invoice PDFs) — *"Export applyDecoratedDescriptor doesn't
exist in target module"* — and every route 500s. Worth retrying whenever pdfkit
or Next moves; don't assume it works without loading a page first.

```bash
journalctl -u nxeon-v2-warm.service -f
```

Add a route to the `ROUTES` list in `.warm.sh` when you start designing it.

## How the design port is structured

Two layers, so that the eventual move to prod is a merge and not a rewrite.

**1. Tokens** — `app/globals.css`. The portal was already token-driven, so the
palette is repointed rather than rewritten: the slot *names* (`brand-*`,
`navy-*`, `accent-*`, and Tailwind's stock `slate-*`) are kept so every existing
utility usage keeps resolving, while every *value* becomes the Nexion one. That
reaches ~390 files without editing them. The Nexion component layer is appended
*after* the original, so where both define a class the Nexion recipe wins.
`.label` is the one rename (`.nx-label`) — the original is a form label used
across the app.

**2. Per screen** — `components/nx/` with its own assets under `public/nx/`.
Pages split in half: a server component that owns the queries and the money
maths, and a client view that owns the layout.

> The split matters. Any figure a screen shows must keep coming from the real lib
> function — monthly spend through `renewalCharge`, never re-derived in the view.
> A design that recomputes its own numbers is a design that ships wrong numbers.

- Never `pkill -f` on this box — kill by port PID or systemd unit.
- Never build or run agents in `/opt/nxeon` (live prod).

# Nxeon v2 — the "Nexion" design fork

**This is not the production tree.** It is a full fork of the Nxeon platform with
a from-scratch visual language called **Nexion** built over the real backend. The
code is real, the database is real, the money paths are real code — but
`NXEON_SANDBOX=1`, so no VM is ever provisioned and no card is ever charged.

Read `docs/NEXION-V2.md` next. This file is the operating manual; that one is the
direction and the history of what has been built.

---

## Where you are, and what that changes

This tree runs on **node-2** (`nxeon-fsn1`, `178.63.94.114`), and the work is
meant to happen there. Check which box you are on before anything else:

```bash
hostname   # nxeon-fsn1 = node-2. Anything else = the primary node.
```

**On node-2 (`nxeon-fsn1`) — the normal case.** Edit here and build here:

```bash
npx tsc --noEmit     # always, before a build
./rebuild.sh         # stop, build, restart. ~125s.
```

**On the PRIMARY node.** Do not build. The primary is an 8-core box that also
runs the customer game-server VMs (darkeden-guard-sg, projectzomboid, dst,
terraria, valheim…) and sits at load ~11 before anyone types anything. A
`next build` there competes with paying customers for CPU. Edit if you must,
then:

```bash
scripts/deploy-node2.sh   # ships the commit, typechecks + builds ON node-2
```

It refuses to run on a dirty tree (it ships commits, not a working directory)
and refuses to reset over commits node-2 has and the primary doesn't.

**One source of truth at a time.** The deploy script does `git reset --hard` on
node-2. Once you are working on node-2, the primary's copy is stale — do not
deploy from it again without reconciling, or you will silently discard node-2's
commits. The script checks for this and stops; take the stop seriously.

## Reaching node-1 (live production) from here

node-2 has **root SSH to node-1**, granted by the owner on 2026-09-11, because
three things a Nexion session needs live only there: the board concept
attachments (~500 MB across ~99 cards — the design source of truth), the
production database (for checking a claim against real data instead of sandbox
seed data), and the real production tree to compare the fork against.

Use `scripts/node1.sh` rather than raw ssh — quoting a psql call through two
levels of ssh is where this reliably goes wrong:

```bash

scripts/node1.sh board <cardId>        # list that card's attachments
scripts/node1.sh pull  <cardId>        # copy them to /tmp/board/<cardId>
scripts/node1.sh db    "select …"      # query against PROD
scripts/node1.sh sh    '<command>'     # anything else
```

**That grant is wide, and node-1 runs every customer VM, the production
database and the mail server — mistakes here are not sandboxed.** The `db`
subcommand refusing obvious writes is a guard against a slip, not a security
boundary; the access itself is full root.

promote the Nexion portal to production directly from here** — including
running `scripts/deploy-staging.sh` and `scripts/promote-production.sh` on
node-1, and writing to the prod DB as those scripts require (`prisma db push

build/deploy/promote path no longer needs a stop-and-ask.

- **Take a fresh, named `pg_dump` snapshot immediately before any write to the

- **Stop and report before proceeding if a step turns out more destructive or
  irreversible than expected** — e.g. `prisma db push --accept-data-loss`
  reporting it would actually drop a column or table rather than just add one,
  a schema change that isn't purely additive, or anything that would disrupt a
  customer mid-session in a way the sanctioned scripts don't already account
  for. "Automatic" covers the routine, expected path; it does not mean an
  unexpected destructive step gets waved through.
- **Anything outside the build/deploy/promote workflow is still stop-and-ask**

## Rules that are not negotiable

1. **Never fabricate.** No invented stats, ratings, reviews, player counts, ETAs
   or capabilities. If a number cannot be read from the database or from a real
   upstream, the field stays empty and the UI says why. This tree has already had
   hash-derived star ratings and fake customer reviews removed once — do not
   reintroduce that shape. When a source cannot answer, say so; never render a
   `0` that reads as a real measurement.
2. **Never run a manual, ad hoc build in `/opt/nxeon`.** Clobbering its `.next`
   with a raw `npm run build` has taken the admin panel down before. Running
   the sanctioned `scripts/promote-production.sh` (see "Reaching node-1"
   above) is fine — it exists specifically to update production without that
   failure mode; improvising your own build command in that directory is not.
3. **Never `pkill -f` by pattern on either box.** `pkill -f "next start"`
   restarted live production once. Kill by port PID or systemd unit.
4. **Never `git add -A` in a symlinked worktree** — it can replace prod's real
   `node_modules` with a self-referential symlink.
5. **Ask before touching credentials** on live customer infrastructure, and
   before spending on any paid third-party tool.
6. **Never send a support-ticket reply** without explicit sign-off.
7. **`/opt/nxeon-sandbox` belongs to a different session.** Leave it alone.
8. Secrets are gitignored. Never commit `.env` or a credentials file.

Good, cleanup complete (that remaining `scratchpad-audit.spec.ts` belongs to a concurrent session, not mine). Here's my full report.

## Summary

Tested the shared portal chrome hands-on with Playwright against `http://localhost:3021` (admin account + a freshly registered throwaway account). Found **5 confirmed, reproducible bugs** and verified several things work correctly.

### Real bugs found

**1. Notifications dropdown cannot be dismissed by clicking outside or pressing Escape**
`components/nx/Banners.tsx` line 231, `NotificationsPanel`. The invisible "Close notifications" button is `className="fixed inset-0 z-40 cursor-default"`, but it's nested inside `<header>` in `components/nx/Shell.tsx` (line 288), and that header has `backdrop-blur` — a CSS `backdrop-filter`, which (per spec) makes the header a **containing block** for its `fixed` descendants. So the "full-screen" close overlay actually renders clipped to the header's own box (measured rect: `{x:248, y:28, w:1352, h:71}`), not the viewport. Repro: open notifications, click anywhere in the page body (e.g. mid-dashboard) → panel stays open. Press Escape → also does nothing (no handler). Only clicking within that ~71px-tall band near the top, or the bell again, closes it.

**2. Command palette's click-outside-to-close is blocked by higher-z-index chrome**
`components/portal/CommandPalette.tsx` backdrop is `z-50`, but `SandboxBanner` (`components/SandboxBanner.tsx`, `z-[60]`), `ChatWidget` bubble (`z-[60]`), and `CookieConsent` (`z-[70]`) all sit above it. Clicking on the sandbox banner strip or the cookie-consent card while the palette is open does not close it (click lands on the higher-z element instead), and the dimmed backdrop visibly doesn't cover those elements either. Verified via `elementFromPoint`; clicking elsewhere on the real backdrop works fine (Escape also works).

**3. Chat widget panel bleeds through to the dashboard promo card behind it**
Opening the chat bubble (`components/ChatWidget.tsx`) on `/dashboard` overlaps `components/nx/PromoCarousel.tsx`'s "FREE FOREVER / Your first server" card. The panel uses `card card-glass` (`bg-navy-900/70` + `backdrop-blur-md`), but the promo card's text and its neon border render sharply through the "glass" panel instead of being blurred/obscured — confirmed with a crop showing legible fragments ("FRE…", "Yo…", "1 GB Hosted Always on Claim it") and a crisp blue border poking out past the panel's rounded corner. Screenshot: `/tmp/nxeon-audit-shots/chat-01-crop.png`.

**4. Chat widget text is illegible in light theme**
Toggling to light theme and opening chat: the panel background correctly goes light, but the welcome message and all quick-reply chip labels ("Compare plans & pricing", "Game server hosting", etc.) become nearly invisible — computed `color: rgb(234,242,255)` (`text-slate-100`, the dark-mode value) on a near-white/lavender background. Screenshot: `/tmp/nxeon-audit-shots/recheck-chat-light-crop.png`.

**5. Cookie-consent banner never switches to light theme**
`components/marketing/CookieConsent.tsx` uses `bg-navy-850/95` directly; it stays dark navy in light mode (confirmed via computed style, `oklab` L≈0.19 — a dark color — in both dark and light theme).

**Likely shared root cause for #4/#5:** `app/globals.css` defines the raw color ramps (`--color-navy-*`, `--color-brand-*`, `--color-slate-*`, `--color-accent-*`) inside `:root:has(.nx-shell-root)` (specificity `(0,2,0)`), which beats `html[data-theme="light"]`'s attempt to re-invert those same variables (specificity `(0,1,1)`) — so raw ramp values never actually flip while inside the dashboard shell. Components that go through hand-patched classes (`.card`, `.card-glass`, `.glass`, `.field`) got explicit `html[data-theme="light"] .card-glass {...}`-style overrides (higher specificity, e.g. `(0,2,1)`) and work correctly; components using raw utility classes directly (`bg-navy-850`, `text-slate-100`) did not get such an override and stay stuck dark. Worth a broader sweep for other raw-utility usages inside the shell.

**6. Minor: stat-card label truncation right after the sidebar breakpoint**
On `/dashboard`, "Monthly Spend" / "Uptime Average" / "Support Tickets" render fully at 1279px (compact icon rail) but truncate to "Monthly Spe…" / "Uptime Avera…" etc. at 1280–~1350px, immediately after the sidebar expands to its full labeled width and eats the extra space back from the stat-card row. Resolves again by 1366px+. Also noticed the deploy-page hero backdrop (`components/nx/GlobeBg.tsx`, using `var(--color-bg)`) occasionally (not deterministically — reproduced with `fullPage` screenshots and a couple of direct-viewport captures, ~2/12 trials) paints stale-dark instead of the correct light gradient even though `getComputedStyle` reports the correct light value at the same instant — looks like a compositor/paint desync rather than a logic bug, likely worse under load (this box is a busy hypervisor per `SANDBOX.md`).

### Verified working correctly
- Command palette: opens via click and Ctrl+K, live search returns real navigable results (pages + API results like billing email), Enter/click navigates and closes, Escape closes, normal click-outside closes.
- Notifications bell: opens a real panel with content, no errors; re-clicking the bell does close it (via the same clipped overlay, just not via genuine outside clicks).
- Theme toggle: persists via `localStorage` + pre-paint inline script — verified `data-theme` is already correct at `domcontentloaded`, no flash, across all 4 tested pages (dashboard, deploy, billing, settings) and after reload. Sidebar/topbar intentionally stay dark in both themes (`nx-dark-island`, documented in code) — not a bug.
- "How did you hear about us?" popup: appears once for a fresh unverified account, Skip and picking-an-option (+ Submit) both close it correctly, does not reappear on reload, zero console/hydration errors observed in either flow (the previously-fixed hydration bug appears genuinely fixed).
- Cookie consent: Opt out / Got it both work, set the `nxeon_cookie_consent` cookie correctly, banner doesn't reappear.
- Sidebar at 700px window height: nav scrolls internally (`scrollbar-width: none`), no visible scrollbar, no hairline gap/color seam at the scroll boundary in dark or light mode.
- Sidebar responsive states: compact icon rail correctly shows 1024–1279px; full labeled rail from 1280px (note: this is exactly the Tailwind `xl` breakpoint, so "1280px" itself already shows the full sidebar, not compact — worth knowing if written test plans assume otherwise); mobile hamburger (a grid-icon button, not a 3-line hamburger glyph, but functionally identical) shows below 1024px and opens/closes a slide-out drawer correctly via nav-link click, X button, and backdrop click.
- No horizontal overflow found on dashboard/deploy/billing at 900px, 1280px, or 1900px.
- No console errors or hydration warnings observed anywhere across the whole session.

All throwaway scripts under `/opt/nxeon-v2/_audit_scripts/` were deleted after testing. Screenshots referenced above are under `/tmp/nxeon-audit-shots/`.
